name: Parloa
h1: Parloa ARR: $50M+ and a $1B-Plus Voice AI Unicorn.
intro: Parloa builds voice AI agents for contact centers — phone lines answered by agents that resolve real customer requests instead of playing menus. The company itself announced surpassing $50M revenue, reached roughly fourteen months from its AI platform launch per Leonis Capital, and raised a $350M Series D after a $1B-valuation round in 2025. The sourced timeline is below.

modelTitle: Price the Conversation, Not the Software Seat.
modelParagraphs: Parloa's product answers the phone: voice AI agents that authenticate the caller, resolve the actual request and hand off cleanly when they shouldn't. The economics that made contact centers a software market — per-minute telephony — carry over, which is why Parloa's revenue scales with conversations handled rather than administrator seats.

Contracts combine a platform fee for the agent-management layer with usage tied to call volume, deployed through enterprise contact-center integrations and a Microsoft partnership. The buyer is the operations executive who already pays per-minute for worse outcomes, which makes ROI math unusually direct for enterprise AI.
revenueMix: Enterprise contracts for deploying and managing voice agents.
Volume-based pricing tied to calls handled.
Microsoft and contact-center integrations extend distribution.

faqs.a: Parloa itself announced surpassing $50M revenue in 2026 — a company-stated figure, not an estimate. Leonis Capital separately charts the company at roughly fourteen months from AI platform launch to the $50M mark.
A $66M Series B in June 2024, a $120M Series C at a $1B-plus valuation in April 2025, and a $350M Series D in 2026, per company announcements and PR Newswire.

An AI Agent Management Platform for contact centers: voice agents that resolve live customer calls end-to-end, plus the management layer enterprises need to deploy, monitor and audit them alongside human agents.

faqs.q: Why Did It Take Off in 2023-24 Rather than 2018?
faqs.a: Parloa was founded in 2018, but phone resolution only became viable when LLMs made natural conversation robust. Once calls actually resolved, contact centers — which already budget per-minute telephony spend — switched budget quickly.
Enterprise platform contracts plus usage pricing tied to conversation volume — aligned with the per-minute cost structure contact-center operators already run.
